fixes.explanation: The reason is sitting right in verse 2: “…because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered through it.” Then comes the last line: “Therefore it will remain shut.” No construction crew, no battle, just the fact that He came through that gate. Friend, that's the whole reason, and the text gives it plainly.

I get the thought, because a shut door can mean somebody's still working on it, like a bakery with the oven off and a ladder in the doorway. But nothing in these verses says a word about building. The LORD gives the reason Himself: “…because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered through it.” So this gate isn't shut because it's unfinished.

Facedown is right. Ezekiel the prophet looked, saw the glory of the LORD filling His temple, and says, “…I fell facedown.” That's what he did when he saw it. Friend, the glory fills the temple, and down he goes.

Asleep would be a strange way to meet this moment, friend. Ezekiel the prophet looked and saw the glory of the LORD filling His temple. Then verse 4 says he fell facedown, which is a different thing from a nap.

That's it. The LORD tells Ezekiel to listen closely to “…everything I tell you concerning all the statutes and laws of the house of the LORD.” He also says to take careful note of the entrance to the temple and all the exits of the sanctuary. He asks Ezekiel to look carefully with his eyes and listen closely with his ears.

Priests is right. God says, “They must not approach Me to serve Me as priests…” They also can't come near any of His holy things or the most holy things. Then God says He will appoint them to keep charge of all the work for the temple (Ezekiel 44:14).

That's the one. God says these Levitical priests, descended from Zadok, are the ones “…who kept charge of My sanctuary when the Israelites went astray from Me…” Because of that, they are to approach Him and minister before Him. They kept charge while Israel went astray.

Egypt never comes up in these verses, friend. God says the priests descended from Zadok are the ones “…who kept charge of My sanctuary when the Israelites went astray from Me…” So what the text tells us they did was keep charge of the sanctuary.
